artifact.export: the built-in artifact.export tool formats only the caller's own already committed reviewed-command receipt as XLSX, escaped standalone HTML or sandboxed PDF; it accepts no caller-supplied rows and does not rerun commands. It returns artifact_id, kind, sha256, size and download_url, as artifact.create does. Exporting the same operation in the same format again returns the artifact already made (same artifact_id); another format makes a new one. Each result field is one field/value row typed like an artifact.create cell: a string is its own text, a whole number an integer cell, another number a number cell, a boolean Yes or No and null an empty cell, while a nested object or array stays compact JSON. A PDF export shares the per-user PDF budget of GET /pdf/ (10 a minute) and returns operation_limit past it. Its refusal and failure codes are in `html_artifacts`.

Read-tool artifacts: a native read tool (table.list, table.read or flow.call) may declare artifact: {title, formats: [xlsx, html, pdf], sheets: [{name, source, columns: [{field, label, format}]}]} in mcp.yaml. It is reviewed contract content, in the contract digest only when declared (a manifest without it keeps its digest). source names an array-of-objects property of the tool's output_schema (and output projection) whose objects are the rows; empty means the table.list rows, or the one object a table.read or flow.call returns as a single-row sheet. Each field must be a scalar property of the rows; format is text, integer, number, money (#,##0.00), percent (the field holds a fraction: 0.0525 shows as 5.25%), date or datetime (ISO 8601 strings, stored as spreadsheet dates) and defaults from the field type; a value that does not fit its format fails the artifact rather than landing as text. Up to 8 sheets of 50 columns; sheet names obey the XLSX rule (31 bytes at most, none of the characters it forbids), and titles and labels carry no control or direction-changing characters.

artifact.create: the built-in artifact.create tool takes {tool, format, arguments?}; it is listed only when the caller may run a tool that declares an artifact, refuses an undeclared tool or format, and re-runs the read through the same grant, scope, input-schema and output-schema gates as a direct call. arguments are only that tool's own inputs, and layout, columns and sheet names never come from the model. It returns artifact_id, kind, sha256, size, download_url and read_completeness: a table.list read is one page, and a partial page is reported and noted in the report.

Formats: XLSX has typed cells, a frozen bold header row and column widths; HTML is a printable branded report (the app's name and theme colour as on the connector pages, generation time, one escaped table per sheet, no-network CSP); PDF prints that report through the same sandbox and prerequisites as artifact.export. A PDF renderer that is missing, fails or runs past its deadline returns unavailable_provider from both artifact.create and artifact.export (artifact.export answers denied only when the receipt is not the caller's). Values are written as declared: a money column renders its field as is in major units (an integer-cents field must be converted by the tool, or not declared money), and an integer above 2^53 loses precision in a spreadsheet number, so declare such an id as text.

Download: GET /api/_mcp/artifacts/{id} requires an interactive, non-impersonated session cookie (never a bearer or API token), then rechecks current owner and tenant, role and immutable original producing-command scopes on every request, verifies stored size and SHA-256 and returns the exact issued bytes; artifact.export also requires current reviewed command scopes. Regeneration promises semantic reproduction; byte retrieval returns the exact issued bytes.

Storage: stored bytes use immutable private manifests bound to owner, tenant (empty only on an app without groups; a group app refuses an empty or "0" tenant), current owner role and immutable original producing-command scopes, operation, source bundle/revisions and template/engine versions. Artifact storage is never reachable through /api/_signed_url, /uploads/ or a serve_file step, even from a record that names its path.

Read artifact retrieval: the stored artifact keeps the producing tool's scopes (plus its flow's), the flow's role (else the caller's role) and operation read:<tool>, so retrieval is the download rule plus three checks specific to a read artifact: it is a snapshot that expires 7 days after creation (same 404 as an unknown id), the current reviewed manifest must still declare the producing tool with an artifact in that format, and for a table tool the caller's current access rule for the table (member-of, owner_or_role, role and so on) must still admit a read, so a user who lost access cannot keep downloading an earlier snapshot; row-level ACLs are not re-run and the 7-day expiry bounds that.

Budgets: 20 artifacts an hour per user in any format (operation_limit), PDFs also draw from the shared PDF budget, at most 5000 rows per sheet, 100000 cells and 16 MiB per artifact, and a user keeps only their newest 25 read artifacts within 128 MiB: when a new one is made, the first artifact (walking newest to oldest) that breaks the count or byte budget or is past its 7 days, and every older one, loses its manifest and bytes (command artifacts are not counted). On local storage the bytes are removed after the commit and any leftover is swept at start-up; on S3 or CDN storage the delete is best effort and can leave an orphan object.
